reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one change to when Codex sessions are woken. A plain codex terminal that joined Codex's shared app-server runs its hooks under that server, which keeps a closed terminal's conversation loaded, idle and clientless for about 30 minutes with no signal Notifai can attribute; a content-free wake there starts a turn nobody sees. Notifai now never wakes an idle Codex session whose host is the shared server (an app-server with --listen, --managed-daemon, daemon or remote-control on its command line, read once per host process). Its answers and notes are still accepted and staged, and the next prompt or tool hook drains them as before; accepts_messages, presence and the SessionEnd classification are unchanged. codex --no-daemon terminals and the Codex app's own server keep the idle wake; an unknown host (Windows, unreadable process) keeps it too. harness-codex.md says the shared-server terminal is never woken while idle and that the answer waits for the User's next prompt there; harness-setup.md qualifies its two wake sentences the same way; README says the same. Doctor's report-only wake-route line for an active shared-server Codex session now says Notifai never starts a turn there while idle and the answer arrives at the next turn; question routing readiness is unaffected (direct_wake_optional). Lifecycle activation text, hook definitions, hook output, hook.gate reasons and domain terms are unchanged; agents do nothing differently beyond not expecting an idle wake there. Skill and lifecycle context budgets remain enforced.
